newsitem.title: USA: FORECAST - US experts watch CPI, retail data 11/11 wk.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - US experts watch CPI, retail data 11/11 wk.

text.p: Consumer prices and retail sales will steal the show next week amid expectations the Federal Reserve's Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) will hold rates steady at its November 13 meeting, economists said.
Based on a separate Reuters poll Friday, all 37 primary dealers surveyed said they see no action by the Fed.
"The Fed is a no brainer," said Kevin Flanagan, first vice president and an economist at Dean Witter Reynolds Inc.
What will draw market players' attention, however, will be consumer prices and retail sales, economists said.
"The more important number is the Consumer Price Index (CPI)," said Dan Seto, senior economist at the Nikko Securities Co International Inc.
"Because (CPI) is more labor intensive, you are likely to see some reflection in the wage increases," added Seto.
On average, 23 pundits foreceast overall CPI rose 0.2 percent in October after a 0.3 percent September rise. Core CPI, which excludes volatile food and energy prices, rose 0.1 percent, they forecast.
"Retail sales are going to be a key number," said Waldo Best, senior economist at BZW Securities Inc.

"Everything else is going to be either offset by something or relatively benign," said Best, adding that retail sales might show a 1.0 pecent increase based orcent increase. Excluding automobiles, retail sales were also up 0.3 percent, they forecast.
The Commerce Department is scheduled to release both the CPI and retail sales on Thursday at 0830 EST/1330 GMT.
